summary: The cursed can slips on segment 0 step 30, then the JavaScript drop path stops because do.c:dropx reaches the ordinary floor tail without the newsym hook. C applies the same cursed-charge branch, drops the can through dropx -> dropy -> dropz, redraws the hero square, and updates encumbrance. The actionable source scope is the partially ported do.c drop family and its production callers.

source.branch: A charged cursed can of grease slips when apply.c:use_grease evaluates (obj->cursed || Fumbling) && !rn2(2). In this recipe the hero is not swallowed, stands on reachable ordinary floor outside a shop or altar, and dropx proceeds through dropy to dropz; the dropz floor branch must complete placement, stacking, newsym, and encumber_msg.
callers: apply.c:use_grease (2604-2654), including the charged cursed-slip branch at 2618-2623; production path js/apply.js:use_grease -> js/do.js:dropx. This is the caller exercised by the assigned session.
do.c:drop (714-780) calls dropx after the command checks; production path js/do.js:drop -> js/do.js:dropx, with dropCommandEnv supplying the drop-tail operations.
do.c:dosinkring (at 514 and 652) calls dropx for ring giveback and a backed-up sink; production path js/do.js:dosinkring -> js/do.js:dropx, also with dropCommandEnv.
invent.c:hold_another_object (1208-1311) calls dropx on its drop_it path; production path js/invent.js:gotoDrop uses the caller-provided dropObject hook.
dependencies: display.c:newsym redraws the floor square after dropz places and stacks the object; js/do.js:dropCommandEnv already supplies the operation, but js/apply.js:use_grease calls dropx with only its state/environment and js/do.js:dropx reaches dropzAdmitted without installing that default.
pickup.c:encumber_msg is called after dropz completes and is supplied by js/do.js:dropCommandEnv; preserve it after the redraw.

Preserve do.c:dropx ordering through freeinv, ship_object, altar handling, and dropy, then do.c:dropz floor effects, placement, impact/shop branches, stackobj, newsym, and encumber_msg. The assigned ordinary-floor branch does not enter shop, altar, liquid, swallowed, or impact conditions.

evidence: The saved queue entry and challenges/evaluations/20261006225046-v24.json at 84d84e111155ac834c43327b7c696055df294349 report 30/34 screens, 2276/2282 RNG calls, and 30/34 cursors; the first failure is stop at segment 0, step 30 with “unsupported drop: missing newsym operation”. The recorded C step for key p shows “The can of grease slips from your fingers”; its RNG log includes rn2(2)=0 at apply.c:2618.

nethack-c/upstream/src/apply.c:2604-2640 defines use_grease: for a charged cursed object and rn2(2)==0 it consumes a charge, prints the slip message, calls dropx(obj), then returns ECMD_TIME. The recorded recipe satisfies this branch, so apply.c is the caller and not the missing behavior.

nethack-c/upstream/src/do.c:786-842 defines dropx, dropy, and dropz. dropx removes the object from inventory, handles shipping and altar effects, then calls dropy; dropy calls dropz; the ordinary floor branch of dropz applies floor effects, places and stacks the object, calls newsym(u.ux,u.uy), then encumber_msg().

At the examined commit, js/apply.js:5241-5259 calls dropx with {...env,state}. js/do.js:1777-1797 normalizes that environment but reaches dropzAdmitted directly without the operation defaults; js/do.js:1861 requires the absent newsym hook. js/do.js:1355-1367 shows dropCommandEnv already supplies newsym and encumberMessage to the command and sink callers. This identifies the missing source-to-caller wiring in the partially ported do.c drop family.
